---
title: "Ruige A"
---

## Question

How do adoption rates compare between cats and dogs at the Long Beach animal shelter?

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
longbeach <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2025/2025-03-04/longbeach.csv")

cats_dogs <- longbeach |>
  filter(animal_type %in% c("cat", "dog"))
```
## Overall adoption rates

```{r}
adoption_rate <- cats_dogs |>
  count(animal_type, outcome_type) |>
  group_by(animal_type) |>
  mutate(adoption_percent = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
  filter(outcome_type == "adoption")

adoption_rate

adoption_rate |>
  ggplot(aes(x = animal_type, y = adoption_percent)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(
    title = "Adoption Rates for Cats and Dogs",
    x = "Animal type",
    y = "Adoption rate (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
24.4% of cat outcomes and 26.2% of dog outcomes were adoptions. Dogs had a slightly higher adoption rate overall. I wanted to see whether this pattern changed depending on how the animals entered the shelter.

## Does intake type matter?

```{r}
intake_adoption <- cats_dogs |>
  filter(intake_type %in% c("stray", "owner surrender")) |>
  count(intake_type, animal_type, outcome_type) |>
  group_by(intake_type, animal_type) |>
  mutate(adoption_percent = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
  filter(outcome_type == "adoption")

intake_adoption

intake_adoption |>
  ggplot(aes(x = animal_type, y = adoption_percent, fill = animal_type)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~ intake_type) +
  labs(
    title = "The pattern changed by intake type",
    x = "Animal type",
    y = "Adoption rate (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
Among strays, dogs had a higher adoption rate than cats, at 26.6% compared with 22.8%. Among animals surrendered by their owners, cats had a higher adoption rate, at 39.3% compared with 26.7%. This suggests that the overall comparison does not show the full picture.

## What about other outcomes?

The adoption rates were relatively close overall, so I compared the other outcomes for cats and dogs.

```{r}
cats_dogs |>
  count(animal_type, outcome_type) |>
  group_by(animal_type) |>
  mutate(percent = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = percent, y = outcome_type, fill = animal_type)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~ animal_type) +
  labs(
    title = "Outcome Distributions for Cats and Dogs",
    x = "Percentage of records (%)",
    y = "Outcome"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
The most common outcome for cats is rescue, at about 28%, and the most common outcome for dogs is return to owner, at about 29%. Euthanasia also made up a larger share of cat records, at about 19%, compared with about 7% for dogs. Although their adoption rates were similar, cats and dogs had different rates in their other outcomes.

Data source: [Long Beach Animal Shelter data from TidyTuesday](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2025/2025-03-04).
